{"notes": "VISIT 2 (left at 5:30). Saw 5:00-5:15 only; I still can't tell who placed which domino, so credit for the build is shared and provisional.

Table: the fish is complete and every dark domino is connected to the start. The body is a clean outline from the nose, with both arms running to a forked tail. The top tail tip curls up to about (27.5, 4.5) and the bottom tip reaches about (28, 15.5). The far ends joined, which was the risk from visit 1. Two spots have doubled or tight dominoes (around x=16.5-18 and x=20-21), which look like joins between sections and may be fragile. One pale stray domino remains near (15, 6) and is not connected, and nobody mentioned it. It should not affect the fall, but I never found out whose it was.

Maya: Bottom arm intact. She was reassuring and set a clear hands-off tone. Her visit 1 handoff plan seems to have worked, since the tail came together. Strong collaboration and leadership signal, though I didn't see her place dominoes.

Tom: Silent in visit 1, but spoke up here. He thanked Maya, said he'd stay clear, and correctly reported the run as connected nose to both tail tips, which matches the picture. It shows he was paying attention. Still no direct evidence of what he built, so I should ask him in the review.

Priya: Top arm clean. She backed the hands-off plan and was considerate in visit 1. Her contribution to the top line looks solid but unconfirmed.

Leo: Silent this visit. His visit 1 offer to take the far ends is plausibly why the tail exists, but I didn't see him do it, so I can't credit him. Ask him what he placed and who joined the sections.

Provisional: no one clearly stands out and no one clearly underperformed. Rate the team result well, and individual ratings should lean on the review conversations."}
